title: regex Module
content_markdown: This module offers matching operations against regular expressions using the powerful [PCRE](http://www.pcre.org/) library.
overview: This module offers matching operations against regular expressions using the powerful [PCRE](http://www.pcre.org/) library.
how_it_works: A text file containing regular expressions categorized in groups is compiled when the module is loaded, storing the compiled PCRE objects in an array. A function to match a string or pseudo-variable against any of these groups is provided. The text file can be modified and reloaded at any time via a MI command. The module also offers a function to perform a PCRE matching operation against a regular expression provided as function parameter.

exported_parameters.name: file
exported_parameters.description: Text file containing the regular expression groups. It must be set in order to enable the group matching function.

exported_parameters.name: max_groups
exported_parameters.description: Max number of regular expression groups in the text file.

exported_parameters.name: group_max_size
exported_parameters.description: Max content size of a group in the text file.

exported_parameters.name: pcre_caseless
exported_parameters.description: If this options is set, matching is done caseless. It is equivalent to Perl's /i option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?i) or (?-i) option setting.

exported_parameters.name: pcre_multiline
exported_parameters.description: By default, PCRE treats the subject string as consisting of a single line of characters (even if it actually contains newlines). The "start of line" metacharacter (^) matches only at the start of the string, while the "end of line" metacharacter ($) matches only at the end of the string, or before a terminating newline. When this option is set, the "start of line" and "end of line" constructs match immediately following or immediately before internal newlines in the subject string, respectively, as well as at the very start and end. This is equivalent to Perl's /m option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?m) or (?-m) option setting. If there are no newlines in a subject string, or no occurrences of ^ or $ in a pattern, setting this option has no effect.

exported_parameters.name: pcre_dotall
exported_parameters.description: If this option is set, a dot metacharater in the pattern matches all characters, including those that indicate newline. Without it, a dot does not match when the current position is at a newline. This option is equivalent to Perl's /s option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?s) or (?-s) option setting.

exported_parameters.name: pcre_extended
exported_parameters.description: If this option is set, whitespace data characters in the pattern are totally ignored except when escaped or inside a character class. Whitespace does not include the VT character (code 11). In addition, characters between an unescaped # outside a character class and the next newline, inclusive, are also ignored. This is equivalent to Perl's /x option, and it can be changed within a pattern by a (?x) or (?-x) option setting.

exported_functions.name: pcre_match

parameters.name: pcre_regex
parameters.description: Regular expression to be compiled in a PCRE object.

exported_functions.description: Matches the given string parameter against the regular expression pcre_regex, which is compiled into a PCRE object. Returns TRUE if it matches, FALSE otherwise.

exported_functions.name: pcre_match_group

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: group to use in the operation. If not specified then 0 (the first group) is used.

exported_functions.description: It uses the groups readed from the text file (see Section 1.6.1, “File format”) to match the given string parameter against the compiled regular expression in group number group. Returns TRUE if it matches, FALSE otherwise.

exported_mi_functions.name: regex_reload
exported_mi_functions.description: Causes regex module to re-read the content of the text file and re-compile the regular expressions. The number of groups in the file can be modified safely.

exported_mi_functions.name: regex_match

return_value.description: Returns "Match" if it matches, "Not Match" otherwise.

exported_mi_functions.description: Matches the given string parameter against the regular expression pcre_regex. Returns "Match" if it matches, "Not Match" otherwise.

examples.code:
opensips-cli -x mi regex_match string="1234" pcre_regex="^1235$"
"Not Match"

exported_mi_functions.name: regex_match_group

return_value.description: Returns "Match" if it matches, "Not Match" otherwise.

exported_mi_functions.description: It uses the groups readed from the text file to match the given string parameter against the compiled regular expression in group number group. Returns "Match" if it matches, "Not Match" otherwise.

examples.code:
opensips-cli -x mi regex_match_group string="1234" group="1"
"Not Match"

### List of User-Agents publishing presence status
[0]

# Softphones
^Twinkle/1
^X-Lite
^eyeBeam
^Bria
^SIP Communicator
^Linphone

### Blacklisted source IP's
[1]

^190\.232\.250\.226$
^122\.5\.27\.125$
^86\.92\.112\.


### Free PSTN destinations in Spain
[2]

^1\d{3}$
^((\+|00)34)?900\d{6}$
configuration_examples.explanation:
The module compiles the text above to the following regular expressions:

group 0: ((^Twinkle/1)|(^X-Lite)|(^eyeBeam)|(^Bria)|(^SIP Communicator)|
          (^Linphone)|(^Snom)|(^SIPp)|(^PJSUA))
group 1: ((^190\.232\.250\.226$)|(^122.5\.27\.125$)|(^86\.92\.112\.))
group 2: ((^1\d{3}$)|(^((\+|00)34)?900\d{6}$))

configuration_examples.title: Using with pua_usrloc
Incorrect groups file
configuration_examples.explanation:
will generate the following regular expressions:

group 0: ((^aaa)|(^bbb))
group 1: ((^ccc)|(^ddd))

Note that the real index doesn't match the group number in the file. This is, compiled group 0 always points to the first group in the file, regardless of its number in the file. In fact, the group number appearing in the file is used for nothing but for delimiting different groups.
